risks.risk: A16 throughput in Safari WebGPU is unmeasured. The planning constant (13k particle-substeps per GPU-ms) sits inside a 3k-44k bracket, so the design point could be off by 4x either way.
risks.mitigation: Phase 0 measures it on the user's phone before anything is built on it. Contingency ladder: room scale (dx 5 cm) as default, 2 substeps for liquid-only scenes, the native Metal track pulled forward. All budgets are expressed as particle-substeps so they rescale mechanically.

risks.risk: Core weakness of the stance: about 12k awake particles at 2.5 cm is roughly 25 L of moving matter with nothing resolved below 5 cm. Mechanisms live almost entirely in the stiff-limit tier and the continuum may feel like scenery.
risks.mitigation: State it openly. Room scale gives about 190 L. Design the sample game around media handling (pour, dig, melt, break), where the continuum is the gameplay. Promotion and demotion keeps stiff parts as real matter. Phase 7 attacks the ceiling.

risks.risk: The implicit pressure solve in 3D with free surfaces may not converge in a fixed small iteration count, or may checkerboard on the staggered layout. Many small dispatches may also cost more than the arithmetic.
risks.mitigation: Warm start, block-local sweeps in threadgroup memory and a 2-level multigrid. Residual reported every tick. Fallback: weakly compressible liquids with a reported Mach number, or a PB-MPM-style compliant iteration. Dispatch overhead measured in phase 0.

risks.risk: Sand and stiff-ish solids need softened elastic moduli (up to 1,000-10,000x for real sand shear modulus), which inflates elastic strain and can look spongy.
risks.mitigation: Keep friction angle, yield and density real. Gate softening on the gravity-strain group staying under 1%. Print the factor on the fidelity card. Use 8 substeps or room scale where it buys real moduli. Multigrid implicit elasticity is the long-term fix.

risks.risk: Partitioned body-matter coupling with one-tick readback lag on the web can go unstable for light bodies in dense liquid (added-mass instability). Grid contact acts at cell distance.
risks.mitigation: An added-mass term in the body solve, a sub-cell SDF collider field and a floating-body benchmark as a gate. Native shared-memory readback removes the lag. Low density-ratio cases are flagged degraded on the web.

risks.risk: MPM numerical fracture and resolution-dependent breaking make destruction depend on dx rather than material strength.
risks.mitigation: Crack-band regularisation so dissipated energy matches the fracture energy. A two-resolution fracture test in CI. Stiff bodies break by bond energy criteria. Reported as a Tier 2 closure, not a derivation.

risks.risk: WebKit specifics: stricter WGSL compiler, reported iOS WebGPU crashes, about 2 GB process kill, requestAnimationFrame halved in Low Power Mode, no haptics.
risks.mitigation: Strict-dialect lint and an on-device pipeline compile check at boot. Footprint under 250 MB. OPFS snapshot and resume as a core feature. 30 Hz presentation as a supported mode. Native host for the long term.

risks.risk: GPU floats are not bit-exact across devices, and same-device repeatability is unproven. Replays and any future multiplayer cannot rely on matter state.
risks.mitigation: Fixed-order gather. Stiff tier and game state on a deterministic CPU path. Replays use an input log plus keyframes with divergence reporting. Rollback and lockstep on matter are a non-goal.

risks.risk: Sustained thermal throttling (published stability 51-84%) may sit below the assumed 60%.
risks.mitigation: The governor ladder (render scale, 30 Hz render, promotion refusal, time dilation) never alters physics. Block sleeping doubles as a thermal feature. The soak test is an exit criterion in every phase from 0 onward.

risks.risk: Scope: a simulation that never becomes a game (Noita spent two years finding one), and every kernel maintained twice (WGSL and CPU reference).
risks.mitigation: A vertical-slice game is a phase 5 exit criterion. Designer tools (budgets, boundary material, telemetry, replay) ship with the API. The reference solver is the test oracle, so the duplicate effort pays for CI without a phone.

risks.risk: Material data provenance and licensing; handbook values carry real scatter.
risks.mitigation: Every parameter stores source, uncertainty and licence. Start from open sources (CoolProp, the 'chemicals' library, primary papers). Unmeasured or fantasy materials are flagged in the fidelity report.

non_goals: Atomistic, quantum or relativistic simulation: 'first principles' here means continuum balance laws plus measured constitutive parameters.
Propagating sound and shock waves, compressible gas dynamics and resolved air flow: air is ambient drag and a vapour reservoir in v1.
Resolved turbulence or real water Reynolds numbers: fine splash and vorticity detail is lower fidelity by construction, and the measured numerical viscosity is published.
Metals, wood, stone or hard plastics as time-resolved continua at real stiffness: they are stiff-limit bodies (rigid, affine or bonded) until they break or melt.
Continuum features thinner than 2 dx: cloth, shells, ropes, gear teeth, threads and surface tension are out of the free closure in v1.
Open or streaming worlds in v1: one matter window (3.2 x 1.6 x 3.2 m tabletop or 6.4 x 3.2 x 6.4 m room).
Cross-device bit-exact matter, rollback netcode or lockstep multiplayer.
Maxwell field solves, detailed chemistry and combustion, wave optics, ray-traced rendering: circuits and motors are lumped models only.
A general-purpose game engine (UI toolkit, asset pipeline, audio middleware, editor suite): this is the physics backbone plus a thin host.
Android, desktop or console product targets: the web build may run there, but nothing is tuned or certified off the iPhone 15.
Using Newton, Genesis, Warp, Taichi or IPC as the runtime: they are offline oracles only.
decisions_for_user: 3D at tabletop or room scale (about 25-190 L of moving matter, estimate), or a 2D world with far more matter and extent (the Noita / Powder Toy route)? This plan assumes 3D; a 2D product is a different, much roomier engine.
Default world scale: Tabletop (dx 2.5 cm, 3.2 m window, finer detail, softer stiffness cap) or Room (dx 5 cm, 6.4 m window, 8x more matter volume, coarser detail)?
Where the demo lives: a new public repository with its own GitHub Pages URL (recommended; leaves your existing PWA untouched and makes macOS CI free later), or a subfolder of the existing site?
Will you pay for the Apple Developer Program (US$99/yr) for the native TestFlight track, and when: right after the web demo, or only if the browser ceiling is actually hit?
What should the first game on top be about: liquids, sand and soil, soft bodies, destruction or heat? This sets the order of the material library and which benchmarks gate first.
When the phone runs hot, what is your preference order: truthful slow motion, 30 fps rendering, or lower visual quality? The engine will not change the physics.
Should games be strict by default (no teleporting or velocity setting unless explicitly unlocked and logged), or permissive by default with strict as an opt-in certification?
Is the engine open-source with a public fidelity report? A public repo is needed anyway for free CI, and openness affects which material data sources can be redistributed.
Is your iPhone 15 on iOS 26 or later, or are you willing to update? Safari WebGPU, and therefore the first demo, requires it.

design:layered-multiscale.name: STRATA - Layered Reality Kernel (Laws and Materials -> Representations -> Solvers)
design:layered-multiscale.thesis:
Reality has one set of laws but no single affordable discretisation. On an A16, explicit steel at 1 cm needs about 9,800 substeps per frame and water about 2,500, against a budget of 2-8, so no one solver can be the substrate. The 2026 state of the art (Newton, Genesis) is multi-solver for the same reason. The permanent part of the engine therefore must not be a solver: it must be the laws and the matter.

STRATA keeps three things separate:
- L, Laws and Materials: balance laws kept as an auditable ledger, constitutive models, typed SI units, and a material database with provenance.
- R, Representations: interchangeable descriptions of the same matter, each with a declared validity regime.
- S, Solvers/backends: an f64 CPU reference oracle, an f32 SIMD CPU production path, and GPU kernels.

Every object is matter with a material. The engine runs the cheapest representation whose validity regime contains the object's current state and changes it when the state leaves that regime. A steel beam is a 6-DoF rigid body until its computed stress nears yield, then rigid plus elastic modes, then elastoplastic FEM, then fractured pieces. Across each hand-off mass is exact, momentum is exact to round-off, and energy is audited.

Why this stance wins on a phone:
- Fidelity is spent only where something is happening, which is the only way "as close to real life as possible" survives a roughly 4 W sustained envelope.
- It can start in Phase 0 as a few hundred rigid blocks on the user's iPhone and grow to bending, breaking, pouring and melting without a rewrite. Each new capability is a representation or solver plugged in under unchanged laws, materials and game API.
- Nothing is admitted until it passes analytical benchmarks and agrees with the neighbouring representation where their regimes overlap. Verification is built into the growth path.
- Games see matter, mechanisms, actuators and sensors, never solvers, so game code survives every fidelity upgrade.

Where the stance is weak:
- Hand-offs are the hardest part: pops, thrash at thresholds, and the awkward fact that stress must be estimated in a body modelled as rigid.
- The layering can become architecture for its own sake before anything is measured.
- Coupling between the CPU mechanism tier and the GPU continuum tier is partitioned and lags by a frame; a single unified solver would give more uniform emergent behaviour inside its (small) window than STRATA does across its seams.
- Total scope (seven representations, two hosts) is years of work, and only the early phases are low-risk.
design:layered-multiscale.first_principles_stance:
Charter: "first principles" means continuum-scale balance laws hard-coded once; all object behaviour enters only through geometry plus constitutive models with measured SI parameters; every discretisation converges to its governing equation at a tested order; every shortcut is declared with a number. It does not mean atomistic simulation.

DERIVED (Tier 0-1; lives in the Laws layer and is shared by every representation):
- Balances of mass, linear momentum, angular momentum and energy, kept as a per-step ledger (kinetic, gravitational, elastic, plastic work, heat, electrical, external, numerical).
- Second law as an admissibility test on every constitutive model (dissipation >= 0, heat flows hot to cold), enforced by unit tests.
- Mass, centre of mass and inertia always computed from density x geometry, never typed in.
- Rigid body as the stiff limit of the same continuum; modal dynamics from linear elasticity (K and M from E, nu, rho); yield onset from the computed stress field against yield stress; buoyancy from integrated hydrostatic pressure; Fourier heat equation; Kirchhoff circuit laws; shallow water as depth-averaged flow with its validity ratio checked.

EMPIRICAL CLOSURES (Tier 2; measured parameters with source and uncertainty; pair properties stored per material pair):
Coulomb friction (static and kinetic), Hunt-Crossley contact dissipation and restitution, Hooke and Neo-Hookean elasticity, J2 plasticity with hardening, Drucker-Prager friction angle and cohesion, Newtonian and Herschel-Bulkley viscosity, Rankine and fracture-energy failure, conductivity, heat capacity, latent heat, DC-motor constants, battery internal resistance.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL (Tier 3; labelled as such): drag and lift coefficients on bodies, rolling and torsional resistance, sub-grid surface tension, unresolved turbulence, crack path at mesh resolution, the stress-screening bound used on rigid bodies.

NUMERICAL COMPROMISES (each has a reported metric):
1. Stiffness clamp: contact and elastic frequency limited to 1/4 of the substep rate (120 Hz at 480 Hz). Reports authored versus effective modulus.
2. Liquids solved in the incompressible limit with a fixed iteration budget. Reports residual divergence and density error.
3. Elastic wave-speed cap for soft solids in the particle tier. Reports real versus capped sound speed. Density, yield stress, friction angle, viscosity and thermal properties stay real; the scaling rule preserves Froude number and strength over rho*g*L.
4. Finite resolution (dx 1-4 cm, at most 16 modes, coarse tets). Reports dx and the convergence order measured in CI.
5. Gauss-Seidel non-convergence. Reports constraint residual.
6. Representation hand-off energy residual. Booked in the ledger.
7. Sleeping, float32, one-frame GPU-to-CPU coupling lag, and numerical viscosity (reported as an effective viscosity from Taylor-Green decay).

REPORTING: every object exposes a FidelityRecord (current representation, tier, authored versus effective parameters, active clamps, residuals). The world exposes the energy and momentum ledger every frame, a debug HUD draws it, and CI publishes a fidelity report per build. Physical dissipation (friction, plastic work, viscosity, Joule heating) becomes heat in the body. Numerical dissipation goes in its own bucket and is never relabelled as physics.

Out of scope by charter: quantum and atomistic, relativity, Maxwell field solves, shocks, resolved turbulence, detailed chemistry, wave optics.
design:layered-multiscale.architecture:
THREE LAYERS, ONE-WAY DEPENDENCIES.

L - Laws and Materials: typed SI quantities; the balance-law ledger; a constitutive library of pure functions (strain, strain rate, temperature -> stress, heat flux, yield, failure); a material database starting with 12 entries (steel, aluminium, copper, oak, rubber, glass, concrete, ABS, ice, water, dry sand, clay); a pair table for friction and dissipation.

R - Representations of the same matter, each with a declared validity regime:
- S0 asleep or static.
- S1 rigid, including reduced-coordinate (Featherstone) articulations.
- S2 rigid plus up to 16 linear modes baked from a quadratic-tet eigenanalysis. Modes below 120 Hz use the exact exponential integrator; higher modes are quasi-static. Yields a stress field.
- S3 elastoplastic FEM: stable Neo-Hookean tets plus J2 plasticity as compliant constraints.
- S4 particle continuum (MLS-MPM with APIC transfers): Drucker-Prager granular, Herschel-Bulkley mud, liquids with a grid pressure projection.
- F0 hydrostatic analytic liquid; F1 shallow-water heightfield.
- N lumped thermal and electrical networks.

S - Solvers behind one contract (step, plus a mandatory residual report):
- REF: f64, scalar, simple; the oracle for every representation.
- CPU: f32, 4-wide SIMD, substepped soft-constraint Gauss-Seidel (the Soft Step lineage), graph-coloured, 8 substeps.
- GPU: WGSL compute for MPM, pressure and heightfield. Every GPU kernel has a CPU twin.

REPRESENTATION MANAGER. Picks the cheapest representation whose regime contains the object's state, from dimensionless indicators with hysteresis:
- S1 -> S2 when a screening bound (joint and contact wrenches through section formulas, x3 concentration factor) reaches 0.2 of yield.
- S2 -> S3 when any sample point reaches 0.8 of yield or deflection exceeds 2% of length.
- S3 -> fracture when the failure criterion holds and released strain energy covers fracture energy x new area. Pieces re-enter S1; debris enters S4.
- S3 -> S1/S2 after stress stays under 0.3 of yield for 0.5 s; the deformed rest shape is re-baked asynchronously.
- Solid -> S4 on melting or unbounded plastic flow; S4 -> frozen aggregate after 30 frames below a kinetic-energy-density threshold.
- Liquid moves between particles, heightfield and hydrostatic by distance from interaction and depth-to-wavelength ratio.

HAND-OFF PROTOCOL (transactional, at a substep boundary): mass moves through an integer ledger and is exact. The target state is fitted to reproduce linear and angular momentum to round-off. Promotions embed exactly. Demotions project, and the lost energy (unresolved vibration) is booked as heat. Each transaction is logged for replay.

INTERACTION PORT (avoids pairwise couplings): every representation exposes surface patches (point, normal, velocity, effective inverse mass, material) and accepts impulses.
- Tier A: all CPU representations are solved together in one substep loop.
- Tier B: the GPU continuum is coupled by partition. Collider primitives or SDFs and velocities go up; per-body wrenches accumulate in fixed-point i32 atomics (order-independent, so momentum closes exactly) and come back one frame later. GPU-side body proxies keep contact two-way within MPM substeps.

LEVEL OF DETAIL. Space: an awake bubble of 15-30 m inside a 256 m world; one 64-cubed MPM window. Time: per-island substeps of 8, 16 or 32; sleeping; 60 Hz thermal; background baking.

DETERMINISM CLASSES. CPU tier: bit-exact across x86-64, ARM64 and WASM. GPU tier: tolerance-level, checkpointed. Gameplay-authoritative mechanisms stay on the CPU.
design:layered-multiscale.frame_budget:
Targets on a cool device, sized so a 0.6 GPU thermal derate still fits 16.67 ms (research budget): GPU <= 10 ms (physics 4.5, render 5.5); CPU physics <= 4 ms wall; main thread < 8 ms; about 4 W; 20-30 minute soak.

TIME. Fixed frame 1/60 s. CPU tier: 8 substeps (1/480 s); flagged precision islands 16-32. MPM: 2-8 substeps from an advective limit of 0.8 cell per substep (deterministic rule). Thermal: 60 Hz (research: explicit conduction at 1 cm is stable to 0.15 s even for copper). Circuits: 480 Hz.

CPU SPLIT (web = one thread; native = 2 P-cores):
- Collision, once per frame with speculative margins: 0.8 ms
- Unified solve (rigid, articulations, FEM share it): 2.4 ms
- Modal: 0.2 ms
- Manager, stress screening, ledger, networks: 0.3 ms
- GPU coupling: 0.3 ms

CPU COUNTS (estimates, derivations shown):
- Rigid: Box3D on an M2 gives 555 stacked boxes per ms per core at 4 substeps (research). At 8 substeps, assuming the solver is 70% of cost: 326. Web: divide by 1.4 for WASM and 1.5 for immature code (both unmeasured assumptions) = about 155 per ms, so about 450 awake boxes or 135 convex hulls (hulls cost 3.3x) in 3 ms. Native, 2 P-cores, mature: 326 x 2 x 3 = about 1,950 boxes or 600 hulls.
- Robots: about 25 microseconds per humanoid step (derived from MuJoCo) x 8 = 0.2 ms per frame each; budget four articulations of up to 30 DoF.
- FEM: about 0.15 microseconds per tet-constraint (assumed about 150 flops) x 2 constraints x 8 substeps = 2.4 microseconds per tet per frame, so about 400 tets per ms, traded against boxes.
- Modal: 64 bodies x 16 modes x 8 substeps x about 20 ns = 0.16 ms.
- Sleeping or static: 20,000 bodies.

GPU CONTINUUM (estimate): design point 64k particle-substeps per frame, default 16k particles x 4 substeps. This sits at the upper edge of the research's conservative range (10-17k particles sustained with a heavy renderer) and below its optimistic 50-100k. The 8k tier is the guaranteed fallback and 32k the stretch; the Phase 0 on-device measurement replaces all three.
- Transfers: quadratic B-splines; particle-to-grid by counting sort plus gather, with fixed-point atomic scatter as an A/B option. About 3.4 ms.
- Grid: dense 64-cubed window with an 8-cubed block activity mask. dx 2 cm gives a 1.28 m cube; 4 cm gives 2.56 m.
- Matter: at 8 particles per cell, 16k particles is 16 litres at 2 cm or 128 litres at 4 cm - a bucket to a bathtub.
- Pressure: one 3-level V-cycle or 16 Jacobi sweeps per substep, <= 1 ms.
- Shallow water: 256 x 256 at 10 cm cells, about 0.1 ms.
- Render, 5.5 ms: forward PBR, instancing, one shadow map, half-resolution liquid surface, about 0.75 render scale.

MEMORY (estimate): particles 32k x 96 B = 3 MB; grid 64-cubed x 32 B = 8.4 MB; bodies 20k x 256 B = 5 MB; baked modes, tets and SDFs about 50 MB; snapshot ring 50 MB; assets about 150 MB. Total under 400 MB; hard cap 1 GB on web; every GPU buffer under 128 MiB.

PRECISION: CPU f32 with the world limited to +/-128 m (ulp about 8 micrometres at the edge); f64 world origins later; REF backend f64; GPU f32 in window-local cell units; mass ledger in integer micrograms.

GOVERNOR (decisions recorded as replay inputs): G1 lower render scale; G2 smaller particle tier for new promotions and a smaller awake bubble; G3 30 Hz presentation; G4 declared half-speed simulation. It never changes substep dt, material parameters or laws.
design:layered-multiscale.platform_and_toolchain:
LANGUAGE AND GPU API: Rust (stable) + wgpu v30 + WGSL. This is the only surveyed stack where one codebase and one shader language reach both Safari WebGPU and native Metal with first-class support. WGSL is written to WebKit's stricter dialect from day one (no textures bound to let, constant arrays of at most 2,047 elements, large tables in buffers). Crates mirror the layers: laws (units, ledger), materials, one crate per representation, solve-ref (f64), solve-cpu (f32 SIMD), solve-gpu, host-web, host-ios, bench, validate.

FIRST ON-DEVICE DEMO (no Mac, no Apple account, no signing):
- The engine lives in a new repository; the existing PWA repo is not touched.
- The Linux container builds wasm32 (single-threaded, SIMD128) plus the WGSL kernels. A GitHub Actions job deploys a static site to GitHub Pages.
- The user opens the URL in Safari on iOS 26 or later (WebGPU is on by default) and adds it to the Home Screen for full screen and wake lock.
- Page 1 is a capability probe: adapter limits and features, cross-origin isolation, core count, memory growth, rigid and MPM-kernel microbenchmarks, and a 20-minute soak logger. It emits JSON for the user to paste back.
- Page 2 is the playable scene.
- World snapshots go to OPFS with persistent storage requested, because iOS kills the tab on memory overuse without signalling device loss.

WEB CONSTRAINTS ACCEPTED FOR PHASES 0-4: one physics thread (Rust WASM threads need a nightly toolchain plus a service-worker header shim on Pages); about 1 GB memory budget; integer-only atomics; 30 fps in Low Power Mode; no haptics; no thermal-state API, so the governor infers load from frame timing.

LONG-TERM PATH (native iOS):
- The same core built as a static library for aarch64-apple-ios, with a thin Swift shell and wgpu on Metal.
- Built and signed on GitHub Actions macOS runners (Xcode 26.6) using fastlane and an App Store Connect Team API key; delivered through TestFlight (builds valid 90 days).
- Requires the US$99/yr Apple Developer Program. A public repo gets free macOS runner minutes; private costs about US$0.062 per minute.
- Native adds both P-cores with NEON (E-cores for background baking), ProcessInfo.thermalState, Core Haptics, larger buffers, and an escape hatch below wgpu for hand-written Metal kernels (float-atomic scatter A/B, 1024-thread groups). Metal 4 is optional; no throughput gain is expected from it.

DETERMINISM TOOLCHAIN: no fused multiply-add, no fast-math, in-house sin/cos/atan2, fixed iteration and insertion order. WASM float semantics are fixed by spec, so the WASM build is the cross-platform reference; x86-64 and ARM64 builds are hash-compared against it in CI.

UNVERIFIED, TO BE MEASURED IN PHASE 0:
- The Safari-versus-native compute gap and the phone's real adapter limits.
- The WASM-versus-native CPU penalty and the cost of shader bounds checks.
- Whether software Vulkan runs the compute kernels headless in the container.
- Whether GitHub macOS runners expose a usable Metal GPU for kernel tests.
design:layered-multiscale.game_builder_api:
MODEL: a game is a set of blueprints (matter plus mechanisms) and controllers that sense and actuate. That is exactly what a robot gets from reality, and the game gets nothing more.

MATTER: a body is a shape (primitive, convex hull or baked mesh) plus a material name from the database. Mass, inertia, stiffness, strength, thermal and friction behaviour follow from the material and are not authored per object. Baking (hulls, modal bases, coarse tets, SDFs) runs offline or in the background.

MECHANISMS: joints are physical parts - revolute, prismatic, spherical, weld, bolt, glue - with bearing friction, backlash, compliance, and a breaking strength derived from material and cross-section.

ACTUATORS (stateful physics, split into transmission and dynamics as MuJoCo does): DC motor (torque constant, back-EMF, winding resistance, rotor inertia reflected through the gear ratio squared), gearbox (ratio, efficiency), linear actuator, spring and damper, heater, brake. They draw from energy sources (a battery with capacity and internal resistance) through a lumped circuit. A flat battery stops the robot.

SENSORS: encoder, IMU, force/torque, contact, strain, temperature, current and voltage, range (ray), fluid force. Noise and latency models are optional.

CONTROLLERS: deterministic callbacks at 60-240 Hz that read sensors and write actuator commands (voltage, PWM, or a setpoint to a built-in PID). The player's finger is itself an actuator: a force-limited spring-damper hand, capped at about 200 N by default.

UNITS: typed SI at the API with compile-time dimension checks. Supported range is declared: objects 1 cm to 10 m, 1 g to 10 t, with a warning above 1:1000 mass ratio inside one island.

QUERIES: raycast, overlap, closest point; read-only ground-truth state; the per-object FidelityRecord; the world energy and momentum ledger; a per-blueprint cost estimate against the reality budget (awake bodies, tets, particles), with explicit refusal or declared degradation.

AUTHORING: declarative text blueprints (materials by name, parametric shapes, joints, wiring); glTF for visuals; MJCF subset import; USD later; an in-app builder in the last phase.

DETERMINISM AND REPLAY: fixed step. A replay is the initial snapshot plus the actuator command stream plus governor decisions. CPU-tier state is bit-exact across phone, web and CI; GPU matter replays within tolerance from periodic checkpoints. Snapshot and restore is first-class and doubles as crash recovery.

NOT ALLOWED IN STRICT MODE: setting position or velocity, teleporting, forces at a distance, changing the mass or material of existing matter, creating or destroying matter mid-simulation, per-object time scale, disabling collision between touching matter.

ESCAPE HATCHES (explicit and audited):
1. Source and sink ports that add or remove matter with ledger entries.
2. An "unphysical" namespace (set pose, set velocity, external wrench, kinematic prescribed-motion bodies). Every call logs the momentum and energy injected and clears the session's strict flag.
3. Declared fictional boundary materials (unbreakable, immovable) for level design, because fully destructible worlds otherwise defeat objectives.
4. Whole-world pause and slow motion only.
5. Forcing or pinning an object's representation, shown in its FidelityRecord.
design:layered-multiscale.validation_plan:
Principle: verification checks the maths against closed forms and manufactured solutions; validation checks the physics against experiments. Both are automated, toleranced and run on every change. A representation or solver is not admitted until its tests pass.

RUNNING WITHOUT AN IPHONE:
1. REF (f64) and production (f32) backends run natively on x86-64 in the Linux container.
2. The same WASM binary that ships runs under a headless runtime; its state hashes must equal x86-64's. CPU-tier bit-exactness is what lets CI trajectories stand in for the phone.
3. GPU kernels run on software Vulkan through wgpu if that works; otherwise they are compared with their CPU twins on a macOS runner.
4. The phone gets a self-test page: a 2-minute subset plus soak telemetry, exported as JSON.

TIER 0 (exact):
- Mass ledger drift = 0.
- Closed-system linear and angular momentum drift <= 1e-5 relative over 10 s (f32), <= 1e-12 (REF).
- Dimension errors fail to compile.
- 10,000-step state hash identical on x86-64 and WASM.

TIER 1 (closed forms):
- Free fall against the exact discrete solution; order 1 confirmed.
- Pendulum period including the amplitude series <= 0.5%; energy bounded within 0.1% over 60 s with no secular drift.
- Dzhanibekov: angular momentum <= 1e-4, kinetic energy <= 0.5% over 30 s.
- 1:1000 mass-ratio chain stretch <= 1%; 10-box stack creep < 1 mm in 60 s.
- Incline slip at atan(mu_s) +/- 0.5 degrees; sliding stop distance v^2/(2*mu*g) <= 2%; sliding-cube energy curve <= 3%.
- Cantilever P*L^3/(3EI) <= 2% (modal), <= 5% (FEM), measured order >= 1.8; first bending mode <= 2%; Euler buckling <= 5%; plastic-hinge collapse load <= 10%.
- 1D conduction <= 1% with manufactured-solution order 2; Stefan melting front <= 5%.
- Hydrostatic pressure <= 2%; Archimedes float depth <= 1e-4 (analytic liquid), <= 5% (particles); Torricelli efflux <= 10%.
- RC time constant <= 0.5%; DC-motor stall torque and no-load speed <= 1%.

TIER 2 (experiments):
- Drop-bounce restitution within 5% of authored.
- Martin and Moyce dam-break front <= 10% RMS.
- Granular column run-out: exponent +/- 0.1, prefactor +/- 20%; angle of repose = friction angle +/- 2 degrees.
- MFIX DEM02 bounce heights.
- Cube-toss dataset: tracked, not gated. Target <= 20% of cube width; fitted research simulators sit at 13.5-25%.

TRACKED AND PUBLISHED (not gated): effective numerical viscosity from 2D Taylor-Green decay; effective versus authored modulus; residual divergence.

STANCE-SPECIFIC GATES:
- Representation equivalence: the same scenario forced into rigid, modal and FEM (and into hydrostatic, heightfield and particle liquid) agrees within 3% wherever regimes overlap.
- Hand-off audit: every transition conserves mass exactly and momentum <= 1e-5, with energy residual < 1% of kinetic energy and fully booked.
- No-thrash: a load hovering at a threshold causes at most one transition per second.
- Production solver trajectories stay within tolerance of REF.

Output: a versioned fidelity report (tests, errors, tolerances, active clamps) published with every build.

roadmap.goal: Prove the Linux-container-to-iPhone delivery loop, measure the real phone, and stand up the Laws and Materials layer with one representation.
roadmap.deliverables: New repo with CI and GitHub Pages deploy. Typed SI units, conservation ledger, 12-material database with provenance. Rigid bodies (sphere, box, capsule, convex hull) with a substepped soft-constraint solver at 8 substeps; f64 reference backend and f32 WASM production backend. WebGPU renderer. Touch 'hand' as a force-limited actuator. Capability probe page with rigid and synthetic MPM-kernel microbenchmarks and a 20-minute soak logger.
roadmap.exit_criteria: The user opens a URL on the iPhone 15 and throws and stacks steel, oak and rubber blocks. 300 awake boxes hold 60 Hz (p95 frame under 16.7 ms) for 20 minutes. Probe JSON is returned with adapter limits, particle-substeps per ms and the WASM penalty. Tier 0 plus eight Tier 1 tests are green; x86-64 and WASM state hashes match over 10,000 steps.

roadmap.goal: Make the engine a place where machines are built from parts, powered and controlled only through actuators and sensors.
roadmap.deliverables: Reduced-coordinate articulations; joints with friction, backlash and breaking strength; DC motor, gearbox, spring, battery and lumped circuits; sensor set; controller API; blueprint format v1; MJCF subset import; snapshot and deterministic replay; strict mode with audited escape hatches.
roadmap.exit_criteria: A motorised rover and a 6-DoF arm, built from blueprints only and driven by voltages, run on the phone. Motor tests pass at 1%; pendulum, 1:1000 chain and Dzhanibekov tests pass. A 60-second replay recorded on the phone reproduces the same final hash in CI.

roadmap.phase: Phase 2 - Solids that bend and yield (first representation switch)
roadmap.goal: Demonstrate the core claim: one object changing representation by need, with audited hand-offs.
roadmap.deliverables: Baking pipeline (quadratic-tet modal bases, coarse tets). Rigid-plus-modes and elastoplastic FEM representations. Stress screening. Representation manager with hysteresis and the hand-off ledger. FidelityRecord and debug HUD. Lumped and field thermal.
roadmap.exit_criteria: Cantilever, first-mode, buckling and plastic-hinge tests pass at their tolerances. Equivalence, hand-off audit and no-thrash gates pass. On the phone a steel beam under rising load goes rigid, then bends, then takes a permanent set, with frame time inside budget.

roadmap.phase: Phase 3 - Breaking and granular matter (GPU tier)
roadmap.goal: Add fracture and the particle continuum, coupled to mechanisms with a closed momentum ledger, under a thermal governor.
roadmap.deliverables: Fracture by Rankine and fracture-energy criteria, splitting FEM into rigid pieces plus debris. GPU MLS-MPM with Drucker-Prager and Herschel-Bulkley models in a 64-cubed window. Partitioned coupling with integer wrench accumulation and GPU body proxies. Freeze and thaw of settled matter. Governor with recorded decisions.
roadmap.exit_criteria: Granular column collapse and angle-of-repose tests pass. Coupling momentum closes to 1e-5. The measured sustained particle tier (target 16k particles at 4 substeps) holds 60 Hz for 20 minutes with a rigid scene active. The beam demo now ends in fracture with mass exactly conserved.

roadmap.goal: Liquids at three levels of detail and heat-driven change of state, all on the same material data.
roadmap.deliverables: Grid pressure projection for particle liquids. Hydrostatic analytic and shallow-water heightfield representations with hand-offs. Buoyancy and viscosity. Melting and freezing with latent heat.
roadmap.exit_criteria: Hydrostatic at 2%, Torricelli at 10%, dam break at 10% RMS, Stefan front at 5%. Density error under 1% at the default tier, reported live. A boat blueprint floats on the phone at the analytically predicted draft within 5%.

roadmap.goal: Remove the browser ceiling without changing the core, laws, materials or game API.
roadmap.deliverables: macOS-runner build, sign and TestFlight pipeline. Two-P-core job system with NEON. Thermal-state governor. Haptics. Optional hand-written Metal kernels. Three-way benchmark (Safari WebGPU, wgpu on Metal, raw Metal).
roadmap.exit_criteria: A TestFlight build runs on the user's phone. CPU-tier replay hashes equal the web build's. Awake-body count is at least 2x the web build. A 30-minute soak stays at thermal state 'fair' or better and uses no more than about 17% battery (4.3 W for 30 minutes of a 12.98 Wh pack).

roadmap.phase: Phase 6 - Builder kit and first game
roadmap.goal: Prove that a game can be built on the engine the way a robot is built on reality, using only the public API.
roadmap.deliverables: In-app builder; blueprint library; telemetry and replay tools; designer boundary materials; documentation including the published fidelity ladder and report; one sample game (build a machine that moves a load across a gap).
roadmap.exit_criteria: The sample game ships in strict mode with no engine changes made for it. A new mechanism can be authored on the phone without code. The fidelity report is public and every feature is tagged with its tier.

risks.risk: Hand-off artefacts: visible pops, energy jumps or thrash when an object changes representation. This is the stance's central risk.
risks.mitigation: Hysteresis thresholds; transactional hand-offs with booked residuals; promotions are exact embeddings; equivalence and no-thrash tests gate every transition; per-object pin override; switching only arrives in Phase 2, after rigid bodies are solid.

risks.risk: Stress in a body modelled as rigid is only an estimate. Screening can miss concentrations (late promotion) or over-trigger (wasted cost).
risks.mitigation: Conservative section-formula bound with a x3 factor; modal stress field as a cheap second stage; calibration against the f64 FEM reference on a corpus of shapes; the screening rule is labelled Tier 3 in the fidelity report.

risks.risk: Architecture before evidence: the three-layer design becomes a framework that is never finished.
risks.mitigation: No abstraction lands without two concrete implementations (reference plus production). Phase 0 ships one representation. Interfaces are allowed to change until Phase 3.

risks.risk: Seams between tiers: partitioned CPU-GPU coupling with a one-frame lag can go unstable for light bodies in dense matter, and gives less uniform emergence than a monolithic solver.
risks.mitigation: GPU-side body proxies; impulse limits enforced by the momentum ledger; an added-mass test (light float in liquid) as a gate; small volumes of attached soft matter stay on the CPU tier.

risks.risk: GPU continuum throughput on Safari WebGPU on an A16 is unmeasured; estimates span 10k to 100k particles.
risks.mitigation: On-device microbenchmark in Phase 0, before any MPM design is frozen; 8k/16k/32k tiers; the engine stays useful with rigid, modal and FEM representations alone.

risks.risk: Real stiffness cannot be time-resolved for steel or water, so promoted metal may look too soft.
risks.mitigation: The elastic regime is handled by modal quasi-statics using the real modulus. FEM is entered only near yield, where plastic flow at the real yield stress dominates. The modulus clamp is bounded so yield strain stays under 2%, and is reported.

risks.risk: WebKit quirks: stricter WGSL compiler, iOS-only WebGPU crashes, tab kill near 2 GB, 30 fps in Low Power Mode.
risks.mitigation: WebKit-strict shader dialect; shader smoke test inside the probe page; 1 GB memory cap; OPFS snapshots with resume; a supported 30 Hz presentation mode; the native host as the durable path.

risks.risk: Thermals: sustained GPU output is 50-85% of peak, and the web build cannot read thermal state.
risks.mitigation: Budgets sized at 60% of cool-device capacity; governor driven by measured frame time; settled matter sleeps; a 20-minute soak is an exit criterion from Phase 0 onward.

risks.risk: No device in CI: all on-device evidence depends on the user's phone and time.
risks.mitigation: CPU-tier bit-exactness makes CI trajectories representative; the self-test page exports JSON; on-device requests are kept short and batched per phase.

risks.risk: Contact realism ceiling: friction and restitution are empirical, and even fitted research simulators miss real cube tosses by 13-25% of cube width.
risks.mitigation: Label contact Tier 2; derive compliant normal contact from material data; publish the cube-toss metric; make no claim beyond what the report shows.

risks.risk: Scope: seven representations and two hosts amount to years of work.
risks.mitigation: Every phase ships a runnable, validated increment. Later phases can be cut or reordered without invalidating earlier ones.

risks.risk: Simulation-first projects often struggle to become games (the Noita and Teardown experience).
risks.mitigation: Boundary materials, strength and energy budgets as natural gating, replay and telemetry from Phase 1, and a sample game as the final exit criterion.

risks.risk: Determinism erosion from the GPU tier, governor decisions and background baking.
risks.mitigation: Governor decisions and bake completions are recorded replay inputs; GPU state is checkpointed; gameplay-authoritative state stays on the CPU tier.

non_goals: Atomistic, quantum or relativistic physics; Maxwell field solves (magnets and motors are lumped models).
Resolved compressible gas dynamics, shocks and explosions; resolved turbulence; detailed combustion chemistry.
Time-resolving the real stiffness of metals or the real compressibility of water. These are declared clamps, not targets.
Light transport or wave optics as part of the physics claim. Rendering is separate, and the A16 has no hardware ray tracing.
Acoustic wave propagation in air. Modal object sound may come later as a cheap by-product of the modal representation.
One universal solver or a single-substrate world. The plan deliberately uses several representations under one set of laws.
Open worlds of kilometres in the first version. The world is 256 m, the awake bubble 15-30 m, and resolved flowing matter is a bucket to a bathtub.
Bit-exact GPU results across devices, and rollback netcode or multiplayer in the first version.
Learned or neural physics surrogates as the authority for behaviour.
A full visual editor comparable to Unity or Unreal; authoring is text blueprints plus a simple in-app builder.
Android, desktop or Pro-only features (120 Hz, ray tracing) as supported targets, although the web build may happen to run elsewhere.
Embedding or wrapping a third-party physics engine as the core. Box3D, Jolt, Rapier, MuJoCo and Newton are references and oracles only.
decisions_for_user: Will you pay for the Apple Developer Program (US$99/yr)? It is required for the native app (Phase 5). Without it the engine stays a Safari web app with one physics thread, about half the body count, no haptics and a roughly 1 GB memory budget. If you buy it early, the native phase can move up to right after Phase 1.

Should the engine's new repository be public or private, and under what licence? Public gets free macOS build minutes and makes the fidelity report open; private costs about US$0.062 per macOS minute. Either way I recommend not putting it in your existing PWA repo.

What should the first game be, and at what scale? My default is a workshop-scale machine and robot sandbox (1-3 m of active matter), which fits the phone's budget best. Vehicles or outdoor terrain would change the resolution and which representations get built first.

Are you willing to be the device lab? Each phase needs you to open a page, run a probe or a 20-30 minute soak, and paste back a block of JSON. Please also say which iOS version the phone runs (26 or later is required) and whether you use a case.
When the phone gets hot, which do you prefer by default: full fidelity at 30 fps, or 60 fps with less matter resolved? The engine will not change physical laws or timesteps either way.

Do you expect to want multiplayer or rollback later? If yes, gameplay-critical matter must stay on the bit-exact CPU tier and GPU-simulated matter cannot decide outcomes; that is cheaper to commit to now.

How strict should games be by default? Strict mode forbids teleports, velocity edits and conjured matter, with audited escape hatches. Should your own games start in strict mode with opt-in exceptions, or permissive with a 'physical purity' score?

redteam:variational-solver-first:feasibi.lens: Performance and delivery skeptic. Re-derived the frame, power and memory-traffic budgets from the supplied research numbers, and inspected the actual Linux container (read-only) for the delivery path. Web search was unavailable (budget exhausted), so checks were derivations plus three direct source reads: the AVBD authors' 3D demo solver, WebKit Performance.cpp, and the PhoneFluid README.

fatal_flaws.flaw: The frame budget is sized so the frame still fits when the GPU is throttled to 60%, not sized to the sustainable power envelope. The combined duty cycle is roughly 1.3-1.9x over what the research says an A16 phone can hold, so the reference scene, the 'about 4 W' figure, the 11% per 20 minutes drain and the 'thermal state at or below fair for 20 minutes' exits cannot all be true. The budget and the governor both have to change: budget from watts, and allow the governor to shed simulated load.
fatal_flaws.evidence: Research numbers: A16 GPU averages 7 W at full load (GFXBench Aztec); sustainable whole-device draw is about 4.3 W (30-minute Genshin run); idle with display is 0.94 W. The plan runs the GPU 10 of 16.67 ms (60% duty, about 3-4.2 W) plus up to 16 P-core-ms per frame (2 x 4 ms physics + 8 ms main thread, about one P-core, roughly 2-3 W) plus display: about 5.5-8 W (my derivation, low confidence on the exact split). A 4.3 W envelope leaves roughly 5-6 ms of GPU and about 5 P-core-ms per frame, about half the plan. The governor's first two steps only cut rendering (30 Hz presentation removes about 27% of GPU time and 0% of physics), so the steady state is 0.5x time dilation, i.e. slow motion. On the web tier the design-point state (thermal mitigation) is exactly when WebKit halves requestAnimationFrame to 30 fps.

fatal_flaws.flaw: The plan's identity (one AVBD-lineage block-descent solver for everything, on CPU, one sweep per substep) rests on a solver with no CPU or mobile measurement, against the research's explicit recommendation (Soft Step baseline, AVBD as a time-boxed R&D track). The decision gate is in Phase 2, after the Phase 1 solver, joints, friction and ledger are built on it, and the stated fallback (a Soft Step velocity sweep for rigid contact) reintroduces the rigid/deformable solver seam the thesis exists to remove, which forces a redesign of Phase 3.
fatal_flaws.evidence: Research: every AVBD implementation is marked experimental, with no CCD, sleeping or bitwise determinism, and no published CPU timing; VBD converges poorly at 1:10,000 stiffness ratios; Catto reports artefacts from deriving velocity from positions. I read the authors' own 3D demo source: it defaults to 10 iterations per 1/60 s step, single precision, no substepping, velocities by BDF1 from positions, so the plan's 4-8 single-sweep substeps is an unpublished operating point (4 sweeps per frame for piles is under half the authors' default). The '2x a Soft Step sweep' cost is an unsupported estimate; my operation count puts 2x as the floor before SIMD losses.

fixable_flaws.flaw: The first on-device milestone bundles delivery proof, device measurement and a full solver v0 (joints, friction, islands, sleeping, ledger, touch hand, 12 tests, hash CI) into one gate, so the cheapest and most decision-relevant data arrives last.
fixable_flaws.fix: Add a Phase 0 measured in days: probe page, one WGSL compute smoke test, block-solve and P2G microbenchmarks, and a 20-minute synthetic-load soak that burns exactly the planned duty cycle (for example 4.5 ms GPU compute + 5.5 ms render + 4 ms CPU) to test the power budget before any solver exists.

fixable_flaws.flaw: The AVBD versus Soft Step A/B gate is in Phase 2 and its 'pre-agreed criteria' are not stated; 'the solver choice is recorded' is not a pass/fail exit.
fixable_flaws.fix: Run the A/B natively on x86 in the container in the first two weeks (no phone needed) with written thresholds: cost per body-substep with SIMD, 10-box stack drift, sliding-cube dissipated energy, 1:1000 chain stretch, momentum defect. Build articulations and deformables only on the winner.

fixable_flaws.flaw: The matter tier is budgeted in particle-passes, but with a dense 64^3 window and gather P2G the cost is dominated by grid cells: 262,144 cells against about 2,000 occupied at 16k points, and about 7.1M neighbour-cell probes per pass against 432k particle-node pairs.
fixable_flaws.fix: Use an active-block list (occupancy mask over 8^3 blocks) or a tight moving AABB of 32^3-48^3, 16-byte fixed-point cells, and budget cell-passes and particle-passes separately. Measure both, plus per-dispatch overhead for the roughly 30-40 compute dispatches per frame, in the Phase 0 microbenchmark.

fixable_flaws.flaw: Phase 4 exit tolerances contradict the plan's own declared softening: hydrostatic within 3%, density error at most 5% at 0.5 m and dam-break front within 10% are not reachable at a 23 kPa effective modulus and 4 passes, so Phase 4 cannot exit as written.
fixable_flaws.fix: Either restate the tests inside the resolvable regime (depth of 0.1-0.15 m at dx 2 cm, dam height of about 0.1 m, tolerance tied to the reported Mach number) or add and price a warm-started volume/pressure constraint solve for liquids, and gate it on a measured density error.

fixable_flaws.flaw: The thermal governor may not touch any simulated quantity, and several exits allow 'or the governor's declared 30 Hz mode', which makes the 60 Hz criteria unfalsifiable. The web tier also has no thermalState API, only frame-rate halving after the fact.
fixable_flaws.fix: Add declared, logged load shedding of simulated amount (matter window and point count through demotion and sleeping, awake-bubble radius) ahead of time dilation. Write exits as 'sim-time ratio 1.0 and at least 95% of frames at 60 Hz, zero dilation events', with a fixed soak protocol (Low Power Mode off, stated brightness, no case, unplugged, ambient noted).

fixable_flaws.flaw: GPU kernels would be developed blind. I checked this container: no /dev/dri, no Vulkan ICD, no lavapipe installed, and a GitHub release download returned 403 through the proxy. WebKit's WGSL compiler cannot run on Linux at all, and with no Mac there is no Web Inspector, so every Safari-only shader failure costs a push, a Pages deploy and a human round trip.
fixable_flaws.fix: Phase 0 tasks: get WGSL executing in the container (software Vulkan from apt, or headless Chromium with a software WebGPU adapter), add a macOS runner job that loads the page in Safari through safaridriver (unverified that the runner exposes WebGPU), and ship an on-page diagnostics overlay that captures compilation info, error scopes and uncaught errors into the copyable report.

fixable_flaws.flaw: The on-device instruments are too coarse for the gates. WebKit's performance.now() defaults to 1 ms resolution (confirmed in Performance.cpp); GitHub Pages cannot be cross-origin isolated without the service-worker shim; GPU timestamps are 'if exposed'. A 4 ms p95 gate therefore carries about 25% instrument error and the 4.5 ms GPU budget is unobservable.
fixable_flaws.fix: Adopt the isolation shim (or a host that sets COOP/COEP headers) from Phase 0 for high-resolution timers, time batches of N ticks rather than single ticks, infer GPU cost from load-ramp tests to the frame-miss point, and print a build hash in the HUD and every report so stale cached builds are detectable.

fixable_flaws.flaw: Single precision is defended only for the increments. Constraint residuals need absolute island-local positions, and at the stiffness clamp one rounding step of position is a non-trivial force, worst in the 16-32 substep precision islands where it matters most. Mueller 2020 and Macklin 2019 both state small steps need double precision.
fixable_flaws.fix: Evaluate constraint residuals in f64 or in contact-local relative coordinates, price precision islands at 1.5-2x for the lost SIMD width, and put a far-from-origin resting-jitter and slow-creep test in the Phase 1 desktop suite before the fp32 decision is frozen.

fixable_flaws.flaw: Per-island substep classes (4, 8, 16-32) create a runtime cost cliff and a stiffness jump. A 32-substep mechanism touching a 4-substep pile forces the merged island to 32 substeps (8x the pile's cost), and because the clamp is a fraction of the substep rate the pile's contact stiffness changes by up to 64x. The budget meter cannot price this statically.
fixable_flaws.fix: Tie the stiffness clamp to one global reference rate so materials do not change with what they touch, cap the size of precision islands, and have the budget meter price the worst-case merge.

fixable_flaws.flaw: Toolchain and hosting set-up is not in the Phase 1 deliverables. In this container rustc 1.97 stable, cargo and Node 22 are present and crates.io, npm and static.rust-lang.org are reachable, but the wasm32 target, wasm-bindgen, wasm-opt and wasmtime are missing, the container is ephemeral, and prebuilt GitHub release binaries appear blocked. WASM threads in Rust also need nightly, which contradicts 'stable toolchain'. A new repository, its Pages enablement and session push access are user-side steps.
fixable_flaws.fix: Make an environment setup script and a pinned tool list the first deliverable (cargo-built wasm-bindgen, Node as the WASM test runner instead of wasmtime), state that the web tier is single-threaded for good unless nightly is accepted, and list the user's one-time steps. The existing repository's workflow at /home/user/pulsevault/.github/workflows/pages.yml shows an Actions-based Pages deploy pattern that can be copied.

fixable_flaws.flaw: A project site in a new repository under the same account shares the github.io origin with the user's existing PWA: OPFS, IndexedDB, storage quota and the persistence grant are origin-wide, so engine snapshots and any 'clear website data' debugging step can collide with or wipe the existing app's local data in Safari.
fixable_flaws.fix: Namespace all storage under an engine-specific directory and database name, never instruct origin-wide data clearing, test through a Home Screen install (separate storage container), or host the engine on its own origin, which would also allow real COOP/COEP headers.

fixable_flaws.flaw: The roadmap has measurable exits but no durations, effort budgets or kill criteria, and some exits test the wrong thing: Phase 2 requires writing a pick-and-stack manipulation controller, and Phase 5 depends on Apple steps that are manual (programme enrolment delay, app record creation in App Store Connect, signing secrets) with a 30-60 minute blind build-and-TestFlight loop.
fixable_flaws.fix: Time-box each phase with an explicit re-plan trigger, replace the cube-stacking exit with an engine-only grasp-hold test (slip under 1 mm for 10 s at a stated grip force), move the Developer Program decision to the end of Phase 2, and have the user place signing keys directly into repository secrets, never in chat.

numbers_challenged.claim: About 4 W device draw with GPU at most 10 ms, CPU physics 4 ms on 2 P-cores and main thread under 8 ms; about 11% battery per 20 minutes.
numbers_challenged.correction: About 5.5-8 W for that duty cycle, i.e. 14-20% battery per 20 minutes and a thermal state above 'fair' well inside the soak. A 4.3 W envelope supports roughly 5-6 ms GPU total and about 5 P-core-ms per frame.
numbers_challenged.basis: Research figures: 7 W average A16 GPU at full load, 0.94 W idle with display, 4.32 W sustained in a 30-minute game run, 12.98 Wh battery. Linear duty scaling with a credit for running at a lower frequency; my derivation, low confidence on the exact split.

numbers_challenged.claim: An AVBD 6x6 block sweep costs 2x a Soft Step sweep, giving about 1,100 stacked boxes native at 8 substeps and about 400 on the web.
numbers_challenged.correction: Plan on 2.5-4x: about 550-900 boxes native and about 130-300 on the single WASM thread, until the A/B measures it.
numbers_challenged.basis: My operation count for a stacked box: about 5,800 flops per AVBD body sweep (16 contact-point visits with 6x6 outer products, LDLT, dual update) against about 2,850 for Soft Step solve plus relax, which matches Box3D's measured 0.315 microseconds. The remainder is SIMD loss from variable-length per-body lists (Box2D data puts SIMD at 1.56-3.5x) and no FMA.

numbers_challenged.claim: The invariant is particle-passes per frame; 16k points x 4 passes on a dense 64^3 grid fits 4.5 ms.
numbers_challenged.correction: Grid traffic dominates: 8.4 MB of grid touched for clear, gather and update gives about 40-70 MB per pass, 160-280 MB per frame, 10-17 GB/s at 60 Hz, which alone can exceed the 4.5 ms budget by about 1.5-2.5x.
numbers_challenged.basis: 64^3 x 32 B = 8.4 MB; 262,144 cells x 27 neighbour probes per gather pass; LPDDR5 theoretical 51.2 GB/s shared with CPU, display and renderer, assumed about half usable by GPU compute (my assumption).

numbers_challenged.claim: Scaling the one measured iPhone MLS-MPM app gives 16k points sustained natively (12k on web) at 4 passes.
numbers_challenged.correction: The transfer is not valid as stated: 16k is the top of the research's 10-17k range, the source's substeps per frame are not published, and its grid is roughly 10-20x smaller than 64^3. Plan 6-8k points x 4 passes or 12-16k x 2 until measured.
numbers_challenged.basis: I read the PhoneFluid README: no substep count, no per-frame milliseconds, no A16 figures. 43k particles at 40% fill and 2.1 mm cells implies about 13-27k cells at 4-8 points per cell (my inference). Combined with the power correction above.

numbers_challenged.claim: Hydrostatic pressure within 3% and density error at most 5% at 0.5 m depth.
numbers_challenged.correction: At the plan's own 23 kPa ceiling the compression at 0.5 m is about 21%. Reaching 5% needs about 98 kPa, i.e. a 9.9 m/s wave speed: more than 8 explicit substeps at dx 2 cm, or dx 4 cm at 4 substeps with zero CFL margin.
numbers_challenged.basis: rho x g x h = 1000 x 9.81 x 0.5 = 4.9 kPa; 4.9/23 = 21%; c = sqrt(K/rho); the 23 kPa ceiling is the research's derived figure for dx 2 cm and 4 substeps.

numbers_challenged.claim: Martin and Moyce dam-break front within 10%; advection limit 3.6 m/s at 3 cm with 2 substeps.
numbers_challenged.correction: A 0.3-0.5 m dam has a front speed of about 3.4-4.4 m/s against a numerical sound speed near 4.8 m/s: Mach 0.7-0.9 where the weakly compressible rule needs under 0.1, and at or above the advection limit. Water falling 0.66 m already reaches 3.6 m/s.
numbers_challenged.basis: Front speed about 2 x sqrt(g x H); free-fall speed sqrt(2 x g x h); the Mach under 0.1 rule is in the research.

numbers_challenged.claim: 0.6 microseconds per FEM vertex-sweep (22 tets x 25 ns); 600 FEM vertices at 4 sweeps native, about 250 on the web.
numbers_challenged.correction: Expect 1.2-2.3 microseconds, and monolithic coupling means the island's 8 (or 16-32) substeps, not 4: about 150-300 vertices native and 60-125 on the web. Four tyres from 250 vertices are about 60 each, a 12-sided wheel with 3.4% radial run-out.
numbers_challenged.basis: 25 ns is about 86 cycles at 3.46 GHz for a stable Neo-Hookean gradient plus 3x3 Hessian block of roughly 300-400 flops, which needs more than 4 flops per cycle without FMA (my estimate). 1 - cos(15 degrees) = 3.4%.

numbers_challenged.claim: Unknowns are increments, so fp32 keeps full relative precision at small h.
numbers_challenged.correction: True for increments, not for constraint residuals: one position rounding step at 4-8 m from the island origin is 0.48 micrometres, which at the stiffness clamp is about 0.27 m/s^2 of force noise per unit mass (3% of g) at 8 substeps and about 4.3 m/s^2 (44% of g) at 32 substeps.
numbers_challenged.basis: k = m x (2 x pi x f)^2 with f = 120 Hz and 480 Hz; float32 spacing of 2^-21 m in the 4-8 m binade; my derivation, order of magnitude.

numbers_challenged.claim: Phase 1 exit: 150 bodies at p95 physics time of at most 4 ms on the phone.
numbers_challenged.correction: The estimate is 1.2 ms only if AVBD is 2x, WASM costs 1.4x and the v0 solver already has tuned SIMD. With 2.5-4x, 1.4-2x and no SIMD the range is about 2-11 ms, and the measurement itself is quantised to 1 ms.

numbers_challenged.claim: Two P-cores scale 1.85x for physics, as on the M2 Air.
numbers_challenged.correction: Expect about 1.3-1.6x on the phone, since the main thread, render submission and the browser or GPU process share the same two P-cores during the 4 ms physics window.
numbers_challenged.basis: The M2 benchmark ran on a machine with four P-cores and no competing render load; the A16 has two. My estimate, to be measured natively.

numbers_challenged.claim: Reference scene costs 3.4 ms, including 2 robots at 0.24 ms each.
numbers_challenged.correction: That prices everything at 8 substeps. A geared robot flagged as a precision island at 32 substeps costs about 0.96 ms each, and any pile it touches inherits 32 substeps. With the corrections above the scene is about 1.7x over 4 ms before the power halving, so a sustainable native scene is roughly one third of the stated one.

numbers_challenged.correction: It saves only rendering: 5.5 ms x 30 fewer frames is 165 ms of 600 ms of GPU time per second (27%), and no physics or matter compute at all.
numbers_challenged.basis: The fixed 60 Hz tick still runs 60 matter and solver steps per second; arithmetic on the plan's own GPU split.

best_ideas: Web-first delivery with a capability probe and on-device microbenchmarks that replace every estimate. The container check supports it: Rust 1.97 stable and Node 22 are installed and crates.io, npm and the Rust distribution host are reachable, so a wasm32 static site is buildable from here.

CPU-authoritative, bit-deterministic core with WASM as the determinism reference, so a replay log captured on the phone reproduces in the Linux container. With no Mac and no attached device, this is the only realistic debugger.

The Reality Report: energy ledger with a 'numerical' account, momentum defect, and a requested-versus-achieved stiffness table per material pair. It turns unavoidable compromises into measured, visible quantities.

A budget meter and CI performance gates expressed in deterministic operation counters (block solves, contact rows, particle-passes, and it should add cell-passes), which work without a phone and survive hardware changes.

Sensors-and-actuators as the only write path in strict mode, with a logged and counted Director API for the non-physical escape hatches, and physical gating levers (battery energy, torque and current limits, material strength).
Twenty-minute thermal soak as a phase exit criterion from the start, settled islands and settled liquid always sleeping, and snapshot plus resume-after-tab-kill treated as a core feature.

Honest scale declarations: bucket-to-bathtub matter, stiff matter rigid with the clamp reported, kinematic gear pairs as the default with real tooth contact deferred, and a fixed cut order so mechanisms never slip.
A solver interface defined as 'energy terms plus block updates' with an A/B harness, which keeps materials, API, ledger and tests intact whichever solver wins. Keep the harness; move it to the front.
redteam:variational-solver-first:feasibi.verdict: Not shippable as budgeted. The delivery path for a first web demo is real and the reporting discipline is the best part of the design, but the frame budget is about 2x over the phone's sustainable power envelope, the matter tier's cost model ignores the grid that dominates it, and several Phase 4 and Phase 5 exit criteria contradict the plan's own declared limits. The central solver bet is unmeasured and gated too late. If this design is kept, it needs a days-long Phase 0 on the real phone (probe, microbenchmarks, synthetic-load thermal soak), the solver A/B run on desktop before anything is built on it, budgets re-derived from watts at roughly half the stated scene, and a governor that can shed simulated load. On those terms the mechanisms tier at a few hundred bodies is credible; the 16k-point matter tier alongside it at 60 Hz for 20 minutes is not yet.

redteam:variational-solver-first:physics.lens: Physics and first-principles skeptic, and game-builder advocate

fatal_flaws.flaw: The charter's one hard-coded law is backward Euler, which does not conserve angular momentum even at full convergence, so the Noether claim is false. It also dissipates stored elastic energy at first order. The time discretisation must change (second-order or variational for resolved conservative terms, or velocity-level constraint impulses); the block solver can stay.
fatal_flaws.evidence: Derivation: a mass held on a circle by any internal force obeys phi -> phi(1 - phi^2) per substep, giving omega(t) = omega0 / sqrt(1 + 2*omega0^2*h*t). I confirmed this numerically with a fully converged solve at 480 Hz: 16% of angular momentum is lost in 1 s at 10 rad/s, 54% at 30 rad/s and 85% at 100 rad/s, identical for 5, 20 and 120 Hz springs and for a hard constraint; at 1920 Hz the losses are still 5%, 28% and 70%. This hits welded or jointed maximal-coordinate parts with offset centres of mass, loop closures, FEM tyres, belts on pulleys and cloth; single rigid blocks and reduced-coordinate tree joints are exempt. The research already said so (MuJoCo: implicit treatment damps tumbling at about (h*omega)^2 per step; rigor notes: keep the conservative part symplectic). Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-pulsevault/a416cf0e-c7c2-56a3-935d-f4967a8e2aae/scratchpad/chk/be_checks.py

fatal_flaws.flaw: One vertex-block Gauss-Seidel sweep per substep breaks action-reaction between interacting bodies, and the defect is solver-order dependent. The plan's own momentum gate (1e-3 of exchanged impulse) is unreachable at the budgeted sweep count. The remedy is pairwise impulse (dual) updates for rigid contact and joints, which is the Soft Step fallback, so the 'one solver' thesis is the part most likely to die.
fatal_flaws.evidence: Body A is solved against B's stale position and B against A's new one, so the penalty forces differ by kappa/(1+kappa) with kappa = k*h^2/m = (omega_c*h)^2 = 2.47 at the declared clamp. A 1D two-body toy with stiffness at the clamp gave a defect of 71% of the exchanged impulse at 1 sweep, 6-21% at 2-4 sweeps and about 0.3% at 10 sweeps; two equal boxes meeting head-on drift off together. For a 1:10 mass pair in the unfavourable order the heavy body received 3.5x the light body's impulse. An AVBD-style penalty ramp cut the defect to 1-26% but only by trading it against 4-16 mm of penetration set by tuned parameters. The contact research recommended Soft Step as baseline and AVBD as time-boxed R&D; the plan inverts that with no new evidence. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-pulsevault/a416cf0e-c7c2-56a3-935d-f4967a8e2aae/scratchpad/chk/ramp.py

fixable_flaws.flaw: The validation plan tests conservation only at benign operating points: one pendulum of about 1 m at about 25 degrees, a single rigid body for Dzhanibekov, and isolated free bodies. It would not catch the spin-down or the launch-energy loss.
fixable_flaws.fix: Add torque-free spinning tests (welded dumbbell, hinged pair, FEM wheel, belt drive) at 10, 30 and 100 rad/s gating angular momentum and kinetic energy. Add spring-launch efficiency at 5-50 Hz, a head-on equal-mass impact and Newton's cradle. Run every test at the shipped substep and sweep budget with sleeping disabled.

fixable_flaws.flaw: Energy-ledger closure at 1e-4 is vacuous if the 'numerical' account is the residual, and nothing caps how large that account may be.
fixable_flaws.fix: Compute the numerical account independently (for backward Euler, half the mass-weighted velocity jump squared plus half the stiffness-weighted position increment squared). Gate numerical loss as a maximum fraction of physical dissipation in every reference scene.

fixable_flaws.flaw: Restitution cannot emerge from Hunt-Crossley under this integrator, so balls, cradles and springboards are numerically dead and the MFIX DEM02 bounce test cannot pass.
fixable_flaws.fix: Add a declared Tier 2 velocity-level restitution closure e(v) per material pair from measured data, or integrate resolvable contact springs with an energy-consistent rule. Reserve Hunt-Crossley for contacts whose frequency is far below the substep rate.

fixable_flaws.flaw: The stiffness clamp and substep count are per island, so physics depends on contact-graph membership: the same pad is 64x stiffer in a 32-substep island than in a 4-substep one, and numerical damping changes with it.
fixable_flaws.fix: Fix one substep rate and one clamp per world, declared by the game. Buy precision with extra sweeps only, and add a substep-invariance test (4, 8 and 16 substeps must agree within tolerance).

fixable_flaws.flaw: AVBD's stabilisation alpha, penalty ramp beta, warm-start decay gamma and post-stabilisation pass are tuned non-physical parameters, and they are missing from the declared compromises. The authors' demo uses alpha 0.99, beta 1e5 (its own comment says the paper suggests 1-1000), gamma 0.99, 10 iterations plus a post-stabilisation pass at 60 Hz, and has no restitution.
fixable_flaws.fix: List them as declared compromises with sensitivity tests (results within tolerance across their ranges), or use fixed material-derived stiffness and pay in sweeps. Budget the post-stabilisation pass explicitly.

fixable_flaws.flaw: Separate static and kinetic friction coefficients make the dissipation potential non-convex, contradicting 'every D is convex', and the normal force is lagged by a substep.
fixable_flaws.fix: Declare friction a non-variational Tier 2 closure. Refresh the normal force inside the sweep, and add stick-slip and friction-limit-under-transient-load tests.

fixable_flaws.flaw: No tests for tunnelling, gear slip under load or joint drift under load, and CCD exists only against statics. 'Gear ratio exact' holds only if the gear is eliminated as a coordinate coupling inside one articulation block.
fixable_flaws.fix: Add bullet tests (1 cm part at 50 m/s against thin dynamic plates and cloth), a loaded gear train over 1,000 revolutions (ratio, backlash, efficiency) and loaded-joint separation limits. Add opt-in dynamic CCD and state the speed envelope as thickness divided by substep.

fixable_flaws.flaw: Bridge: 'stiffer than the clamp is rigid' is decided by material modulus, so structures become rigid bodies with hard welds whose redundant load paths are set by solver order. Finite-strength welds are in the API but fracture is Phase 7 and first on the cut list.
fixable_flaws.fix: Decide rigidity by structural mode frequency: a 1 m steel bar of 1 cm^2 carrying 100 kg sits near 71 Hz, which is resolvable. Give members derived lumped compliance (EA/L, EI) through rods and shells, move breakable welds to Phase 2-3, and test a redundant truss against the stiffness method.

fixable_flaws.flaw: Vehicle: there is no enclosed-gas energy term, so a tyre cannot be pneumatic. FEM tyres in the inertial frame suffer the rotational spin-down, and rigid wheels with Coulomb friction have no slip curve. A differential needs a three-shaft constraint that the gear pair does not provide.
fixable_flaws.fix: Add a pressure-volume (ideal gas) energy term as a primitive. Solve tyre and belt deformation in the rim's co-rotating frame, add a declared brush-tyre closure for rigid wheels, and add three-shaft gear constraints.

fixable_flaws.flaw: Boat: the charter forbids any buoyancy formula while the matter tier holds 16-128 L, so a boat is a toy in a tub and cannot travel.
fixable_flaws.fix: Add a Tier 1 analytic hydrostatic reservoir: integrate rho*g*z over the wetted hull against a height-field free surface (this is Archimedes, not a fudge), with wave-making and drag declared Tier 3. Embed the particle window in it for near-field detail.

fixable_flaws.flaw: Fire is absent from all seven phases: no gas phase, no combustion, no smoke, and heat conduction only in Phase 7.
fixable_flaws.fix: Either declare fire a non-goal or add a Tier 3 slice. That slice is solid heat conduction pulled forward (explicit and cheap), one-step pyrolysis with measured ignition temperature and heat of combustion, and a coarse Boussinesq gas grid sharing the GPU matter budget, with mass and energy booked in the ledger.

fixable_flaws.flaw: CPU-GPU coupling lags one frame, which acts as negative damping of about omega*tau/2 (0.075 for a 0.7 s heave). The impedance term is a stabiliser with no reaction on the fluid, and a 2% per-exchange gate allows secular drift.
fixable_flaws.fix: Derive the impedance from GPU-measured displaced mass and reconcile predicted against actual impulses so the net is zero. Gate cumulative drift (a floating body at rest for 60 s) and consider same-frame readback for small windows.

fixable_flaws.flaw: API: 'mass and inertia never authored' conflicts with MJCF import and with real parts (hollow shells, internal motors). The controller-only write path makes every game designer a controls engineer, there is no character path, and the SDK arrives in Phase 6.
fixable_flaws.fix: Accept measured mass properties with provenance and consistency checks. Ship a controller library (joint servo, wheel speed, inverse kinematics, balance) as ordinary strict-mode code, and expose a usable SDK from Phase 2.

fixable_flaws.flaw: The A/B gate sits in Phase 2, after the v0 solver and articulations are built on AVBD, and its pass criteria are not stated.
fixable_flaws.fix: Move it to Phase 1 with criteria fixed in advance (momentum, angular momentum, cost per body, stack drift). Box3D has an Emscripten build, so run it on the phone as the measured Soft Step baseline instead of writing a second solver.

fixable_flaws.flaw: FEM fidelity at phone resolution: linear tets lock in bending and near incompressibility, and under-converged sweeps soften global modes. Matter tests can pass at CI resolution while the shipped configuration was never validated.
fixable_flaws.fix: Use rods and shells for slender parts and a locking fix (F-bar, mixed or quadratic elements) for rubber. Require every structural and matter test to run at the shipped resolution, particle count and pass count with its own published band.

numbers_challenged.claim: Pendulum energy loss at most 0.5%/s at 480 Hz (estimate 0.3%/s from 0.75(theta-dot*h)^2 per substep).
numbers_challenged.correction: The formula is a cycle average and 0.3%/s needs peak angular speed near 1.4 rad/s (a 1 m pendulum at about 25 degrees). Loss scales as 0.75*theta-dot-max^2*h per second: a 25 cm pendulum at 60 degrees loses about 6%/s, and continuous rotation at 10 rad/s loses 29% of its kinetic energy in the first second.
numbers_challenged.basis: Derivation of the projection map plus numeric check at 480 Hz.

numbers_challenged.claim: Momentum defect of interacting islands at most 1e-3 of exchanged impulse per tick, with one sweep per substep.
numbers_challenged.correction: About 71% at clamp stiffness with 1 sweep, 6-21% at 2-4 sweeps, about 0.3% at 10 sweeps. Meeting 1e-3 in one sweep needs kappa below 1e-3, a contact frequency under about 2.4 Hz at 480 Hz.
numbers_challenged.basis: Defect = kappa/(1+kappa), kappa = (omega_c*h)^2 = 2.47; 1D two-body toy.

numbers_challenged.claim: An AVBD 6x6 block sweep costs 2x a Soft Step sweep, giving about 1,100 stacked boxes native and about 400 on web.
numbers_challenged.correction: Unsupported; plan on 3-6x, which gives roughly 400-780 boxes native and 150-300 on web. If conservation needs about 10 sweeps per substep the count falls by a further order of magnitude.
numbers_challenged.basis: Each row is assembled twice into a dense 6x6 with ragged per-body row counts that defeat 4-wide SIMD; I recomputed the plan's own cost model with factors 3 and 6.

numbers_challenged.claim: Hunt-Crossley contact dissipation replaces a restitution constant.
numbers_challenged.correction: A contact spring with zero physical damping returns a coefficient of restitution of about 0.05 at the clamp frequency, 0.51 at 30 Hz and 0.80 at 10 Hz (480 Hz substeps). Raising the substep rate does not help because the clamp scales with it.
numbers_challenged.basis: Backward Euler keeps 1/(1+(omega*h)^2) = 29% of modal energy per substep at omega*h = pi/2; numeric check.

numbers_challenged.claim: Springs and stored elastic energy are first-principles terms in Psi.
numbers_challenged.correction: A spring launch delivers 90%, 79%, 60% and 33% of its stored energy at 5, 10, 20 and 50 Hz (480 Hz), about 2% lost per Hz. Catapults, bows and pogo mechanisms are off by tens of percent.
numbers_challenged.basis: Loss over a quarter period is (pi/2)*omega*h; numeric check.

numbers_challenged.claim: Liquid density error at most 5% at 0.5 m depth, with the P-wave modulus topping out near 23 kPa.
numbers_challenged.correction: rho*g*h/K = 4.9 kPa / 23 kPa, about 21%. Reaching 5% needs K of at least 98 kPa (sound speed about 9.9 m/s), which is 9 or more explicit substeps at dx 2 cm against 4 budgeted passes.
numbers_challenged.basis: The plan's own modulus and the hydrostatic relation.

numbers_challenged.claim: 600 FEM vertices (about 2,500 tets) at 4 sweeps natively, 250 on web; soft tyres from measured E.
numbers_challenged.correction: The default is 8 substeps in the same sweep, so 300 vertices native and about 125 on web. At 2 cm elements a 120 Hz clamp caps E near 60 kPa, about 80x softer than tyre rubber at 5 MPa.
numbers_challenged.basis: Highest element frequency is about 2c/dx with c = sqrt(E/rho) and rho = 1,100 kg/m^3 (my assumption that the clamp applies to element modes).

numbers_challenged.claim: Rolling and torsional resistance scaled by the computed contact-patch radius.
numbers_challenged.correction: If the radius comes from the clamped modulus it is 27-126x too large. It must be computed analytically from the real moduli, independent of the numerical clamp.
numbers_challenged.basis: Hertz: a scales as E^(-1/3); 2e11 Pa clamped to 1e7-1e5 Pa.

numbers_challenged.claim: Archimedes draft within 5% at dx 2-4 cm.
numbers_challenged.correction: Grid-distance contact offsets the hull by about half a cell (1-2 cm), so 5% needs a draft of at least 10 cells (20-40 cm). That does not fit in 16-128 L; the test passes only at CI resolution.
numbers_challenged.basis: Research note that MPM contact acts at grid-cell distance, plus geometry.

numbers_challenged.claim: Supported range: parts down to 1 cm at speeds up to 50 m/s.
numbers_challenged.correction: At 480 Hz a body travels 10.4 cm per substep and CCD covers statics only, so dynamic-dynamic tunnelling is possible for anything thinner than about 10 cm. Offset-bound cloth contact is valid only up to radius/h (2.4 m/s for an assumed 5 mm radius).
numbers_challenged.basis: Arithmetic on the plan's own substep rate.

best_ideas: The Reality Report: an always-available HUD and JSON with the energy ledger, momentum defect, requested-versus-achieved stiffness table, density error, coupling defect and a count of non-physical Director actions.
Strict mode with a logged Director escape hatch, where spawned mass and energy are booked as external and prescribed-motion bodies report their power draw.

The machine-shop API: materials with provenance and uncertainty, a material-pair table, parts, assemblies, actuators, sensors and fixed-rate controllers, with battery energy, torque limits and material strength as the designer's gating levers.
DC motor physics done properly: K_t = K_e, back-EMF as a Rayleigh dissipation term K^2/R, reflected rotor inertia N^2*I, and battery internal resistance through nodal circuit analysis.

Reduced-coordinate articulations with exact tree joints as first-class bodies. They are also exempt from the backward-Euler spin-down, which is a second reason to route every revolving mechanism through them.
Bit-deterministic CPU core with WASM as the reference, so a replay captured on the phone (including recorded GPU wrenches) reproduces in the Linux container in place of an attached debugger.
A thermal governor that only touches rendering, presentation rate and logged time dilation, never dt, substeps or iterations, with every workload sized to 60% of cool capacity.
Phase 1 as a capability probe and microbenchmark on the user's actual phone, with the measured numbers replacing the estimates before anything is committed.
A budget meter that prices an assembly in block solves, contact rows and particle-passes before it runs, and performance CI gated on those deterministic counters.
Fidelity tier tags on every feature, phone-resolution error published beside refined error, and the cube-toss dataset kept as an honesty metric.
An explicit A/B gate against Soft Step behind an 'energy terms plus block updates' interface. Keep the gate; move it earlier.
Attached deformables solved on the CPU in the same loop as their mechanism, with bulk matter on the GPU behind a recorded coupling interface.
